newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia Cargo pledges more Malpensa use.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia Cargo pledges more Malpensa use.

text.p: Alitalia is ready to operate out of Milan Malpensa airport's cargo city as soon as suitable logistical connections to the hub are completed, said its chief operating officer Domenico Cempella.

Speaking at a cargo transport conference held in Milan, he said that once these requirements had been met, the Italian state airline would by using Malpensa be ready to satisfy the needs of Italian freight companies.
These, he said, were currently required to truck their shipments hundreds of kilometres to meet flights departing from inter-continental airports in Europe.

According to data provided by Roberto Zucchetti, transport consultant to the Italian Chambers of Commerce's Lombardy section, which organised the conference, air cargo passing through Milan's Linate and Malpensa airports declined by 16 percent last year from the 1995 total of around 200,000 tonnes.
The Lombardy section has asked Alitalia to concentrate its inter-continental cargo connections on Malpensa.
